description:
TPO 399 A1 Group of Hornbeam Group to sectional dismantle using  rigging equipment the medium group (Right side of property, rear garden).1x Oak (Right side of property, rear garden) Reduce over-extended branches by 1-2 metres length reduction, growing toward and over garden area. Group of  Hornbeam (Left side of property, rear garden) Sectional dismantle using rigging equipment the declining TG4 Hornbeam group. 1x Oak / Hornbeam group (Neighbouring left rear garden) Reduce over-extended branches up to 3 metres length reduction, growing toward and over garden area. 2x Hornbeam group (left side + right side front of summer house) Sectional dismantle using rigging equipment

Copsewood Estate Northwood: 
1x Coniferous Tree to reduce over extended branches up to 2m length situated in the rear garden right hand side.
application_type_full: Tree works: Trees in conservation areas/subject to TPOs
decision_conditions: The trees are located in the front and rear garden of 70 Copse Wood Way, Northwood. The mature trees provide significant canopy cover, contribute to the arboreal nature of the area, and collectively have a high amenity value.
This application has been refused as no arboricultural justification has been provided and the proposed work is is likely to negatively affect the collective amenity value of the trees.
Dead / dangerous branches may be removed under exemption.
Having regard to the reasons given for the proposed work, the work is unjustified and will have a detrimental impact on the visual amenity and arboreal character of the area.
The removal of deadwood, dangerous / hanging branches and ivy:  This does not require the formal consent of the Council.

Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981:  Note that it is an offence under this act to disturb roosting bats, nesting birds or any other protected species.  Therefore, if applicable, it is advisable to consult your tree surgeon / consultant to agree an acceptable time for carrying out the approved works.
